chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Fazalah ibn Ayoub, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) dyeing with henna, a red dyeing.

key_terms.قَانِيًا: red (specifically the red color of henna)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) do with henna?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the aesthetic preference of Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) for henna, specifically noting the 'qani' (deep red) hue, which underscores the Sunnah of maintaining a youthful and clean appearance. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary textual basis for the recommendation (mustahabb) of using henna for men, distinguishing it from mere permissibility by emphasizing the Prophet's family's active practice. The specific mention of the color also connects to broader Islamic traditions regarding the beautification of the self as an act of worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,
‘I saw Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> dyeing with the henna, a red dyeing’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ibn Khalid from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “
I saw abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, had applied hair dye with henna of red color.’”
